domain_specific_rationale: From a data architecture and financial ledger perspective, the Two-Phase Credit Settlement protocol guarantees ACID consistency for credit balances across asynchronous, multi-stage rendering workloads: 1) Relational Ledger Integrity: Phase 1 executes an atomic reservation (status = 'RESERVED', estimated_cost_credits) within a single PostgreSQL transaction using row-level locking (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), preventing race conditions, balance underflow, and double spending; 2) Settlement / Release Guarantee: Phase 2 commits the exact cost (actual_cost_credits) upon job completion or releases the reserved allocation if the job terminates in FAILED or CANCELLED status; 3) Audit Trail Persistence: Both estimated and actual credit fields are recorded directly in generation_jobs, ensuring full relational reconciliation and auditability against the credit ledger history.
capability_impact: Protects CAP-01 (Canonical Core State) and CAP-08 (Resource & Cost Management), ensuring zero double-spending, accurate billing reconciliation, and transparent audit trails.
residual_risk: Orphaned reservations resulting from ungraceful worker crashes require periodic reconciliation cron jobs (RECONCILED_TERMINAL after lease expiration) in avf-core-state. Fully covered by state machine lifecycle specs.
